title: std/imaging-finding@1
description: What a reader saw, and where. Never a diagnosis and never an effect: this is what a named clinician is shown before they decide, and the writing is a separate motor.* step behind the gate. Coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the frame they sit on, so they survive a viewer resizing, a different rendering and a thumbnail -- pixels would be true only for the exact image that was sent. `limitations` is required for the same reason `findings` may be empty: a reader that cannot say is more useful than one that always says something.

findings.description: Empty is an answer: nothing this reader can point at.

label.description: What it is, in the language of the request.

note.description: Why the reader says so, on this image.

instance_uid.description: The image it is on. A finding that cannot name its image cannot be drawn, and one drawn on the wrong image is worse than none.

box.description: Normalised rectangle of the frame: origin top-left, 0..1 on both axes.

confidence.description: How sure the reader is. Reported because it is asked for, and it is a model's own estimate rather than a measured rate -- whoever draws it should say so.

correlation.description: How the frames relate to each other and to the report on file, including where the reader disagrees with it.

impression.description: The draft a clinician edits and signs. Never written to a record from here.

limitations.description: What cannot be said from these frames: the sample, the plane, the window, what would need another study.
